statement: A distributed operation may declare typed selector parameters whose values come from the authorized invocation arguments and are bound through the canonical SQL parameter path; partition planning and local SQL use the same normalized parameter set, SQL text remains immutable, unknown or type-invalid parameters fail before dispatch, and the code-first compiler generates the declaration without exposing raw Binding names or SQL concatenation. Verified at HEAD 761dc17c7: no such mechanism exists — the invoker plans shards only from the Binding's static WHERE clause (planShards in call-cell-batch-executor.js) and per-call arguments flow only as untyped argumentsJson into the guest.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn an independent verifier before audit and handoff and record its stable evidence id.

The Binding remains the owner of statement shape and permitted parameters; the call invoker, batch executor, and service-source contract remain the owners of dispatch, planning, and code-first declaration. No second planner or alternate statement builder.

Use an explicit authoring construct (declared parameter slots or a typed predicate descriptor); do not enable sql template string interpolation. The caller cannot choose a table, column, operator, tenant, or arbitrary SQL; planner and partition-host executor receive byte-identical normalized values; parameters participate in Binding digest/version fencing.
Evidence must come from a code-first generated service on the public path; raw Binding JSON tests are diagnostic only and cannot satisfy doneWhen.

The scenario must include a red-on-revert proof that restoring full scatter (removing narrowing) fails the local-read/rows-scanned metric, and must define and test nulls, numbers, strings, ranges, and missing values.
